title: Cardano Basics
description: How well do you know the fundamentals? Ada, lovelace, Ouroboros, and Cardano's development phases.

questions.question: What is Cardano?
options: A decentralized proof-of-stake blockchain platform
A centralized payment company that issues its own bank cards
A proof-of-work cryptocurrency mining network
A single smartphone wallet app for storing cryptocurrencies
questions.explanation: Cardano is described in its own documentation as "a decentralized third-generation proof-of-stake blockchain platform," meaning no single company or authority controls it. It secures the network through staked ada rather than the energy-intensive mining used by proof-of-work systems like Bitcoin. The "third-generation" label reflects that Cardano was built after Bitcoin and Ethereum, incorporating lessons from both, and it is a platform, not a company, a mining network, or a single app.

questions.question: What is ada?
options: Cardano's native cryptocurrency, used for fees, deposits, and staking rewards
A separate blockchain that runs alongside Cardano
The name of Cardano's official mobile wallet app
A stablecoin pegged to the US dollar
questions.explanation: Cardano's documentation calls ada "the native, or principal currency on Cardano," the main payment unit used to pay transaction fees, make deposits, and pay out staking rewards. It is not a separate chain, a wallet app, or a stablecoin, it is Cardano's own built-in currency.

questions.question: What is a "lovelace" on Cardano?
options: The smallest subunit of ada, where 1 ada equals 1,000,000 lovelace
A larger denomination equal to 1,000 ada
The official name of Cardano's block explorer
A type of Cardano stake pool
questions.explanation: Just as a bitcoin splits into 100 million satoshis, ada splits into lovelace, its smallest unit, with one ada equal to 1,000,000 lovelace. This fine granularity, six decimal places, lets Cardano handle very small payments and fees precisely. The unit is named after Ada Lovelace, the same person ada itself is named after.

questions.question: What makes native tokens on Cardano different from tokens like Ethereum's ERC-20?
options: Native tokens are handled directly by the Cardano ledger and don't require a smart contract to exist or transfer
Native tokens can only be created by the Cardano Foundation
Native tokens automatically expire after one year
Native tokens can only be traded on a single official Cardano exchange
questions.explanation: On Cardano, custom tokens are a built-in ledger feature, so creating and moving them needs no smart contract. That is unlike ERC-20 tokens on Ethereum, which rely entirely on smart contract code for accounting and transfers. This removes a layer of complexity and reduces the risk of smart contract bugs affecting a simple token transfer. Native tokens can still be used inside smart contracts for things like DeFi, but they don't require one just to exist.

questions.question: The name "Ouroboros" for Cardano's consensus protocol comes from what?
options: An ancient symbol of a serpent or dragon eating its own tail
The surname of the engineer who wrote the first Cardano whitepaper
A Greek word meaning "unbreakable chain"
The name of the first Cardano stake pool
questions.explanation: Cardano's documentation explains that the protocol is named after the ancient symbol, usually a serpent or dragon eating its own tail in a closed circle, with the word itself deriving from Ancient Greek for "tail eating." It is a fitting image for a blockchain: a continuous, self-sustaining cycle. The name is symbolic, not a person's surname or a made-up marketing term, and its real Greek meaning is "tail eating," not "unbreakable chain."

questions.question: What is Ouroboros?
options: Cardano's proof-of-stake consensus protocol
Cardano's official hardware wallet
The programming language used to write Cardano smart contracts
A Cardano-based decentralized exchange
questions.explanation: Ouroboros is the name of the consensus protocol underlying Cardano, described in Cardano's documentation as "the first provably secure proof-of-stake protocol." It is the mechanism that decides which stake pool gets to create the next block, not a wallet, a programming language, or an exchange. Charles Hoskinson adopted the name in 2017 for this specific protocol.

questions.question: How does Cardano's proof-of-stake consensus differ from Bitcoin-style proof-of-work?
options: Block creators are chosen based on stake rather than by winning a computational mining race
Proof-of-stake requires more electricity than proof-of-work
Proof-of-stake blocks are created by a single central server
Proof-of-stake has no way to select who creates the next block
questions.explanation: In proof-of-work, miners compete to solve a computational puzzle first, which uses large amounts of electricity and hardware. In Cardano's proof-of-stake system, the creator of a new block is instead chosen through a combination of random selection and how much stake, meaning ada, they control. Cardano's documentation cites this as far more energy efficient than mining. Selection is distributed across many independent stake pools, not a single central server.

questions.question: What did the Byron development phase establish for Cardano?
options: The foundational proof-of-stake network that allowed users to buy and sell ada
Smart contract support for building decentralized apps
A treasury system for community-funded proposals
Interoperable sidechains connected to the main Cardano chain
questions.explanation: Byron laid the technical foundation, later phases brought stronger decentralization and smart contract functionality. Cardano's documentation states that Byron "set the foundation for Cardano development allowing users to buy and sell ada on a proof-of-stake blockchain network." Stronger decentralization came with Shelley, which "introduced a decentralized ledger creating a completely new economic system," and smart contract functionality came with Goguen. Neither of those capabilities existed yet in Byron.

questions.question: What was the main focus of the Shelley development phase?
options: Decentralizing the network by shifting block production to community-run stake pools
Adding smart contract functionality
Launching Cardano's official mobile wallet app
Introducing native tokens
questions.explanation: Cardano's documentation describes Shelley as the theme that "introduced a decentralized ledger creating a completely new economic system," moving block production from centrally run nodes to a network of independent, community-run stake pools. Smart contracts and native tokens arrived later, in Goguen. Shelley is the development phase most closely tied to staking and delegation as they exist today.

questions.question: What capability did the Goguen development phase bring to Cardano?
options: Smart contract support and custom token issuance
The original proof-of-stake network launch
A community-controlled treasury and voting system
Decentralization of block production across stake pools
questions.explanation: Cardano's documentation describes Goguen as focused "on the establishment of a global, financial, and multi-functional system for decentralized application (DApp) building, smart contract support, and custom token issuance." That is when developers gained the tools to build DeFi apps and other smart-contract-based projects on Cardano. Decentralization of block production had already happened in the earlier Shelley phase.

questions.question: Cardano's development phases (Byron, Shelley, Goguen, Basho, Voltaire) are named after what, with one exception?
options: Poets and writers, except for Goguen, which is named after a computer scientist
Ancient Greek gods
The people who founded Cardano
Cities where Cardano conferences were held
questions.explanation: Cardano's documentation states that its development phases are "all named after poets except for Goguen, a computer scientist." The page draws this poets-versus-scientist distinction as the naming pattern across the five phases, without naming the individual poets or the computer scientist involved. None of the phases are named after Cardano's founders or Greek gods. Cardano's public roadmap site refers to these same five names as "eras" (for example "the Shelley era").

questions.question: Who is the ada cryptocurrency named after?
options: Ada Lovelace, a 19th-century mathematician regarded as the first computer programmer
Charles Hoskinson, one of Cardano's co-founders
A figure from Greek mythology
The Cardano Foundation's first chairperson
questions.explanation: Cardano's own materials state that ada "is named after Ada Lovelace: a 19th-century mathematician who is recognized as the first computer programmer, and is the daughter of the poet Lord Byron." This is a different namesake from the Cardano platform itself, which honors a different historical figure, Gerolamo Cardano. None of the other options had any role in choosing ada's name.

questions.question: The name "Cardano" comes from which historical figure?
options: Gerolamo Cardano, a 16th-century Italian physician and mathematician
Ada Lovelace, a 19th-century mathematician
Charles Hoskinson, Cardano's co-founder
A fictional character invented for marketing purposes
questions.explanation: The platform is named after Gerolamo Cardano, a 16th-century Italian physician and mathematician. That is a different namesake from ada, which is named after Ada Lovelace. The blockchain simply borrows his name, he lived centuries before it existed.

questions.question: Which three organizations are referred to as Cardano's pioneer entities?
options: Input Output, the Cardano Foundation, and EMURGO
The Cardano Foundation, the Ethereum Foundation, and Bitcoin Core
Google, IBM, and Microsoft
A single company called Cardano Inc.
questions.explanation: Cardano's own governance documentation calls EMURGO, Input Output, and the Cardano Foundation the pioneer entities of Cardano, describing them as having "relinquished the genesis keys of the blockchain, handing a more mature governance system to the community." The three are independent organizations, Cardano was never the product of a single company, and none of the other listed organizations were involved.

questions.question: In what year did the Cardano blockchain and ada launch?
questions.explanation: Cardano's genesis block "launched the Byron era on September 29, 2017," which is when the blockchain and ada went live. That is several years after Bitcoin, which launched in 2009, and Ethereum, which launched in 2015, reflecting Cardano's later, research-first approach. 2021 is well after Cardano's launch, it corresponds instead to the rollout of smart contracts in the Goguen era.
